policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV reads only 'where Lazarus was, whom Jesus raised from the dead'; it renders no appositive 'who had died' for ὁ τεθνηκώς, so the shorter reading stands.
ASV names the subject ('whom Jesus raised'), which excludes the omission (r02), but English cannot show whether the Greek name carried the article.
'one of them that sat at meat with him' renders the partitive genitive identically with or without ἐκ.
Μαριάμ and Μαρία are spelling variants of one name; ASV 'Mary' renders either. The only note is an alternative_rendering about 'liquid nard'.
ASV opens 'But Judas Iscariot'. Throughout this chapter ASV renders οὖν 'therefore' (vv. 1, 3, 7, 9, 21, 34); the adversative 'But' answers δέ.

ASV's order 'Judas Iscariot, one of his disciples' and its lack of 'son of Simon' exclude RP's τῶν μαθητῶν-first form with Σίμωνος (r02); the remaining readings differ only by ἐκ, which the partitive English does not show.
ASV subordinates the clause with a participle, 'and having the bag took away what was put therein', rather than the finite coordinated 'had the bag, and took away' of εἶχεν καί.

ASV 'Suffer her to keep it against the day of my burying' makes the keeping the purpose of leaving her alone, a ἵνα clause; RP's asyndetic 'she hath kept it' would leave no complement for 'Suffer her'.
ASV 'to keep it against the day of my burying' is prospective, matching the aorist subjunctive τηρήσῃ; the perfect τετήρηκεν would have given 'she hath kept it'.
The variant is only the article before ὄχλος; ASV 'The common people therefore of the Jews' supplies English 'The' either way, and οὖν ('therefore') is common to both readings.

The mapped textual_variant note, 'Some ancient authorities read the common people. See verse 9', puts the articular ὁ ὄχλος πολύς (rendered 'the common people' at v. 9) in the margin, not the text; ASV's text 'a great multitude' is the anarthrous reading.
The article before the participle is invisible in ASV's 'that had come to the feast'; the verse's textual note concerns the article on ὄχλος, not this one.
ἐκραύγαζον and ἔκραζον are both imperfects of shouting; ASV 'cried out' renders either.
ASV 'even the King of Israel' renders the connective καί (epexegetic 'even') with the article; RP's omission would end the quotation at 'the name of the Lord'.
ASV opens 'These things understood not his disciples'; a transitional δέ is routinely left unrendered, so its absence in English does not exclude it.
Both readings are the same words in different order; 'his disciples' renders either.
ASV 'For this cause also the multitude went and met him' renders καί with 'also'.
ASV 'for that they heard' uses a plural verb, matching plural ἤκουσαν rather than singular ἤκουσεν agreeing with ὄχλος.
ASV 'lo, the world is gone after him' has no 'whole' to render ὅλος.
The readings differ only in the order of Ἕλληνές and τινες; ASV 'certain Greeks' renders either.
A Greek article on the personal name is not shown in ASV's 'Andrew'.
ASV 'Andrew cometh, and Philip' renders the verb ἔρχεται and has no 'again' for RP's πάλιν.
ASV coordinates the final clause, 'and they tell Jesus', rendering καί before λέγουσιν; RP's asyndeton would give 'Andrew and Philip tell Jesus'.
ASV 'And Jesus answereth them' is present tense, matching ἀποκρίνεται, not the aorist ἀπεκρίνατο ('answered').
ASV 'He that loveth his life loseth it' is present, matching ἀπολλύει; the future ἀπολέσει would give 'shall lose it', which ASV reserves for the following 'shall keep it'.
Word order only; 'If any man serve me' renders either arrangement of τις and διακονῇ.
ASV begins the second condition without a connective, 'if any man serve me, him will the Father honor', rendering ἐάν alone rather than καὶ ἐάν.
The readings differ only in where the subject stands; ASV 'Jesus answered and said' renders either.
Attributive and predicate order of the demonstrative are both rendered 'This voice' in ASV.
ἐάν and ἄν with the subjunctive are orthographic equivalents here; ASV 'if I be lifted up' renders either.
ASV 'The multitude therefore answered him' renders οὖν with 'therefore'.
Word order of the pronoun with the verb; ASV 'how sayest thou' renders either.
ASV 'We have heard out of the law that the Christ abideth for ever' renders ὅτι with the complementizer 'that'.
ASV 'the light among you' with the margin 'Or, in' gives the range of ἐν ὑμῖν; μεθ᾽ ὑμῶν would be 'with you', which ASV does not offer here.
Temporal ὡς and ἕως are both rendered 'while' in 'Walk while ye have the light'.
As in v. 35, 'While ye have the light' renders either ὡς or ἕως.
The variant is only the article before the name; ASV 'spake Jesus' shows no article either way.

ASV contrasts tenses within the verse: 'He hath blinded their eyes, and he hardened their heart'. The simple past answers the aorist ἐπώρωσεν; the perfect πεπώρωκεν would have given 'hath hardened' to match the preceding perfect.
Simple and compound verb alike are rendered 'And should turn'.
ASV's 'And I should heal them' continues the μή clause and reads the same whether the Greek is future indicative or aorist subjunctive.
ASV 'because he saw his glory' is causal, rendering ὅτι; the temporal ὅτε would have given 'when he saw'.
ASV 'hear my sayings, and keep them not' renders φυλάξῃ ('keep'), not πιστεύσῃ ('believe').
ASV 'he hath given me a commandment' is perfect, matching δέδωκεν rather than the aorist ἔδωκεν ('gave').
Word order of the emphatic pronoun with the verb; ASV 'which I speak' renders either.
